info.title: Flow API
info.summary: REST API of the Flow issue tracker
info.description:
Flow's HTTP API. Typed operations (with request and response schemas reflected from the server's Go types) form the public contract; every other route is listed as an inventory entry that may change.

Authenticate with a personal API key or an OAuth access token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; tokens select their workspace. Browser sessions send the `X-Workspace-Key` header.
Lists return connections (`nodes`, `pageInfo`) paged with `first`/`after` or `last`/`before`, ordered newest first by `orderBy` (createdAt or updatedAt), filtered with a `filter` object.
Routes marked `x-flow-internal` serve the web app and are not part of the contract. Payloads Flow sends to webhook endpoints are described in the `webhooks` section.
Errors use one envelope (`error`, `code`, `type`, `requestId`). Requests are rate limited per user or application (X-RateLimit-* headers, HTTP 429 with type RATELIMITED).
The API is unversioned: changes are additive, deprecated operations are flagged and kept for at least six months. See docs/api.md.

get.description: Cursor-paged issue query over an indexed keyset, at most 100 per page. patch.description: The path takes the issue's id, identifier, or an identifier it had before it moved to another team. Fields not listed in the request schema are rejected with 400. teamId moves the issue to another team; the caller needs access to that team (guests cannot move issues). The issue gets the target team's key and a new number (previousIdentifiers keeps the old identifiers, which still resolve), the target team's status of the same name and type (else the first of that type, else its default), leaves its cycle, replaces team-scoped labels by the target team's labels of the same name (dropping the others), and loses its estimate when the target team does not use estimates. Sub-issues stay in their teams.

get.description: The team's memberships with role and origin (manual, invitation, api, sync or scim; memberships from before origins were tracked are manual). By team id or key.

delete.description: Without origin, removes the member like team settings do (not the last owner, not SCIM-managed members). With origin, removes only a membership with that origin (409 TEAM_MEMBER_ORIGIN_MISMATCH with the actual `origin` otherwise) and never an owner (409 TEAM_OWNER_PROTECTED). put.description: Adds the user (role member or owner) or changes the role of an existing member. origin (manual, api or sync) is stored on the membership; without it, API keys and OAuth applications add members with origin api. Giving an origin for an existing member replaces it (audited as origin_changed). SCIM-managed memberships cannot be changed (409).
put.summary: Add a team member or change their role

post.description: members lists the user ids or emails that belong on the team. Missing users are added with origin (default sync); members not listed are removed only when their origin is in removeOrigins (default: the sync's origin). Owners and SCIM-managed members are always kept, and manual members are never removed unless removeOrigins lists manual. dryRun writes nothing and returns the same lists.
post.summary: Sync a team's members with a directory

ActorBot.description: ActorBot attributes a record to an OAuth application ("<User> via <App>").
